NDT training in Tampa: how it works for Tampa employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based training for Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET for Tampa Bay employers and technicians. We have no classroom in Tampa. Theory runs live online or in scheduled classroom cohorts, and practical work runs onsite at your facility under ASNT Level III oversight. Certification is issued by your employer under its written practice, not by a training school.

That last point matters more in Tampa Bay than people expect. The work here is spread across very different owners: phosphate and fertiliser plants in Hillsborough and Polk counties, power stations around the bay, ship repair on the Port Tampa Bay waterfront, aerospace and electronics manufacturers in Pinellas County, fuel terminals feeding the Central Florida pipeline system, and FDOT bridge and structural steel work across a metro that keeps building. Each of those employers writes its own written practice, names its own codes and decides which methods and levels it will certify. A course certificate on its own does not make anyone certified. What it does is give the employer's Level III the documented classroom hours they need before on-the-job experience, examinations and a vision test lead to certification.

So the useful question for a Tampa technician is not "where is the nearest NDT school?" but "which methods do the employers I want to work for actually certify, and how do I get the documented hours they accept?" For a Tampa employer, the question is "how do we get our crew through classroom hours and examinations without pulling them off a scheduled outage or a ship in dry dock?" This page answers both, method by method.

If you already know what you need, request a Tampa training quote. We reply with dates and a cohort or onsite quote within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Tampa

Every course below follows the topical outlines of ASNT SNT-TC-1A and is built so the hours can be documented against your written practice. The table maps each method to the kind of Tampa Bay work it usually supports. It describes typical local demand and is not a list of any employer's requirements.

MethodLevelsWhat Tampa employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic testing)I, II, III prepThickness surveys on acid-service piping and tanks at fertiliser plants, weld examination on terminal and power piping, hull plate gauging during ship repairNone for Level I; Level II builds on Level I plus documented experience
PAUT (phased array)II, III prepWeld examination on new-build and repair piping, corrosion mapping where a single-point thickness grid misses localised attackUsually UT Level II under the employer's written practice
TOFD (time-of-flight diffraction)II, III prepThick-wall welds on pressure vessels and power piping, crack sizing alongside PAUTUsually UT Level II
RT (radiographic testing)I, II, III prepWeld radiography on process and power piping, fabrication-shop pressure work, pipeline tie-ins at fuel terminalsNone for Level I; state radiation-safety requirements apply separately for anyone handling sources
MT (magnetic particle)I, II, III prepCranes, lifting gear and port structures, ship repair welds, rotating equipment shafts during power-plant outagesNone for Level I
PT (liquid penetrant)I, II, III prepStainless and non-magnetic components in chemical and fertiliser service, aerospace and precision parts made in Pinellas CountyNone for Level I
VT (visual testing)I, II, III prepWeld and structural inspection on bridges and buildings, pre-examination visual on every other method, tank and vessel internalsNone for Level I
ET (eddy current)I, II, III prepCondenser and heat-exchanger tubing at power stations and process plants, aerospace surface-crack inspectionNone for Level I

UT is the method most Tampa Bay candidates should look at first. Phosphate fertiliser production relies on sulfuric and phosphoric acid, and acid service is hard on piping, tanks and heat exchangers. Plants measure wall loss on a schedule, and the people taking readings, setting up the equipment and signing the report have to be qualified. Level I covers basic physics, straight-beam thickness work and calibration. Level II adds angle-beam weld examination, discontinuity evaluation against acceptance criteria, and writing instructions for Level I staff.

PAUT and TOFD are Level II-and-above courses. They make most sense for technicians already holding UT Level II who want to move into weld and corrosion-mapping work that pays better and is harder to staff. Employers usually set UT Level II as the entry requirement, and your own written practice has the final say.

RT training covers film and digital radiography, exposure calculation, image quality indicators and interpretation. Florida is an NRC Agreement State, so radiation-safety licensing for crews using sealed sources is handled by the Florida Department of Health's Bureau of Radiation Control. The NDT course teaches the method. It does not replace the separate radiation-safety training and radiographer certification the state requires before anyone handles a source.

MT, PT and VT are the fastest routes into paid work for a newcomer. Ship repair, crane inspection, structural steel and plant maintenance all use them daily. ET is more specialised. In Tampa it mostly means tube inspection during power-station and process-plant outages, plus surface-crack work for the aerospace and precision-manufacturing suppliers north and west of the bay.

Level III candidates can take our ASNT Level III exam preparation, which covers the Basic examination topics and method-specific preparation. All courses are listed on the NDT training programmes page.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Tampa, step by step

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, certification belongs to the employer. The sequence below is the same whether you work at a fertiliser plant in Riverview, a ship repair yard on the channel or a fabrication shop in Plant City.

  1. Your employer's written practice sets the rules. This document states which methods and levels the company certifies, the minimum training and experience hours, how examinations are graded, who the responsible Level III is, and how recertification works. If your employer does not have one yet, it needs one before it can certify anyone.
  2. Complete formal classroom training in the method and level. This is the part Atlantis delivers, live online, in a classroom cohort or onsite. The hours you need are set by the written practice, which usually follows the SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums. Check the training requirements matrix rather than relying on a figure someone quotes you.
  3. Build documented on-the-job experience. Experience hours in the method, logged and signed, are what turn classroom knowledge into a qualified technician. In Tampa that experience often builds quickly around outage and dry-dock peaks, as long as someone keeps the log.
  4. Pass the general, specific and practical examinations. The general exam tests method theory. The specific exam tests your employer's procedures, equipment and the codes it works to. The practical exam is done on real specimens with real flaws. All three are administered by, or under the direction of, a Level III.
  5. Pass the vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast checks, repeated at least annually under most written practices.
  6. Receive certification from your employer. The certification record is signed off by the employer's certifying authority, normally on the Level III's recommendation. It is valid for work done for that employer.
  7. Recertify on schedule. SNT-TC-1A sets a maximum recertification interval, and the written practice can make it shorter. Keeping records current is what keeps a technician employable when the next outage mobilises.

Our SNT-TC-1A training and certification guide covers each step in more detail, including what to do when you change employers and your previous certification does not transfer automatically.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Tampa crews

Atlantis has no physical training centre in Tampa or anywhere else, and we would rather say so up front. Tampa employers get three delivery options.

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led sessions in real time, with questions and worked examples. Suitable for the classroom portion of most methods and levels, and for anyone on rotating shifts who cannot sit in a room for consecutive days. See NDT training online.
  • Classroom cohorts. Scheduled when enough candidates need the same method and level, held at an arranged venue.
  • Onsite at your facility. The instructor comes to your plant, yard or shop and uses your equipment, procedures and, where possible, your own flawed specimens. For a Tampa employer with several people to qualify, this is usually the most efficient option, because practical training matches the components your crew actually inspects.

Tampa scheduling runs to its own calendar. Power stations around the bay plan outages outside the summer peak, when air-conditioning load keeps generators running. Fertiliser plants take their own maintenance shutdowns. Ship repair work depends on dry-dock bookings. Hurricane season from June through November can move all of these. We build cohorts around those windows. Theory can run online in the weeks before an outage so candidates arrive trained, and practical sessions can be booked for the quieter weeks afterwards.

Tell us your headcount, methods, levels and preferred window, and we will send an onsite or cohort proposal for your Tampa crew. Employers training several technicians at once should read about our corporate NDT training programmes.

Where NDT technicians work in Tampa

Tampa Bay's inspection work is spread over more sectors than most Gulf Coast cities. That diversity is good for technicians, because one set of certifications can move between industries, and it also means the codes change from one site to the next.

Phosphate and fertiliser. Central Florida's phosphate region reaches from Polk County to the bay, and processing and shipping facilities sit on or near the water. Sulfuric acid plants, phosphoric acid trains, evaporators, storage tanks and conveying equipment all need regular thickness surveys and weld inspection. Plant piping is generally built and repaired to ASME B31.3, and pressure equipment to ASME Section VIII with examinations performed to ASME Section V.

Power generation. Utility generating stations around Tampa Bay, including large gas-fired units that replaced older coal capacity, run boilers, heat-recovery steam generators, condensers and high-energy piping. Outage NDT covers UT and RT on welds, ET on condenser and feedwater-heater tubes, and MT on rotating equipment. Power piping is typically built to ASME B31.1.

Port, terminals and ship repair. Port Tampa Bay handles bulk fertiliser, fuel and general cargo, and the waterfront includes ship repair yards. Fuel terminals feed petroleum products inland by pipeline, so API 1104 pipeline welding and tank inspection sit alongside marine work. Ship repair NDT follows classification-society rules and, for government vessels, the relevant federal specifications. Marine terminals regulated under the Maritime Transportation Security Act generally require a TWIC card for unescorted access, so technicians should check that early.

Aerospace, defence and manufacturing. Pinellas County has a long-established aerospace, defence-electronics and precision-machining base. Aerospace employers often work to NAS 410 or equivalent customer schemes on top of, or instead of, SNT-TC-1A, and some local employers also ask for those qualifications. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based, so if your contract names NAS 410, check with your Level III whether our classroom hours can be credited. MacDill Air Force Base hosts an air refuelling wing. Military NDI personnel qualify under Air Force technical orders, and veterans leaving that career field often convert their experience into civilian SNT-TC-1A certification.

Bridges, buildings and infrastructure. FDOT bridges across the bay, highway flyovers and a steady stream of high-rise construction all generate structural steel inspection. That work runs on AWS D1.1 for structures and AWS D1.5 for bridges, with VT, MT and UT as the main methods. Some local employers also ask fabrication-side staff for AWS CWI, a separate scheme Atlantis does not train for.

Radiography licensing in Florida. Florida regulates radioactive materials and radiation machines through the Department of Health, Bureau of Radiation Control, under Chapter 64E-5 of the Florida Administrative Code. A radiography company needs a state licence or registration. Individual radiographers must meet the state's training and certification requirements, and radiographer's assistants have their own training rules. Out-of-state crews coming in for an outage need reciprocity. Your company's radiation safety officer owns that process, but technicians should understand that NDT certification and radiation-safety certification are separate credentials.

For pay ranges by level and method, see our NDT salary guide rather than any single local figure.

Level III services and written practices for Tampa NDT companies

Many Tampa Bay NDT service companies and in-house inspection departments are small: a handful of Level IIs, a busy owner and no full-time Level III. That is workable under SNT-TC-1A, provided the company has a compliant written practice and access to a Level III who administers examinations and keeps certification records auditable.

Atlantis supports employers in three ways:

  • Written practice development and review. We draft or update your written practice so that it matches the methods you actually perform, the codes your Tampa clients name, and the current edition of SNT-TC-1A. See written practice development.
  • Outside Level III services. Examination administration, procedure review, technique approval and certification-record audits for companies that do not employ a Level III full time.
  • Audit readiness. When a fertiliser, power or aerospace client audits your NDT programme, they ask for the written practice, training records, experience logs, exam results and vision tests. We help you close gaps before the audit.

If you are building or repairing an NDT programme, book a Level III consultation for your Tampa company. The SNT-TC-1A guidance page explains how the pieces fit together.

Practise before the practical exam

Practical examinations are where most first-time candidates lose marks. They rarely fail on theory. They lose marks on calibration, scanning technique and recording. The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 NDT methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Tampa candidates, the tank and oil and gas environments are closest to terminal and plant work, and the hangar environment suits aerospace-bound candidates.

To be clear, the simulator is for practice only. It does not replace the practical examination, which must be done on real specimens with real discontinuities under a Level III. It is a way to arrive at that exam already fluent in the sequence. For written-exam preparation, work through our UT Level 2 practice questions and the similar sets for other methods.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Anoop designs the course content to SNT-TC-1A topical outlines and oversees practical sessions and examinations as the responsible Level III. Tampa employers who book onsite training work directly with him on scope, specimens and the written-practice fit.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Tampa

How do I get NDT certified in Tampa?

Choose a method your target employers use (UT, MT and VT are common starting points in Tampa Bay), complete formal training for Level I, build documented experience, and pass your employer's general, specific and practical examinations plus a vision test. Under SNT-TC-1A your employer then certifies you. Atlantis provides the training and, for employers, the Level III examination support.

Can I take NDT training online in Florida?

Yes, for the classroom portion. Atlantis runs live online theory for all eight methods. The practical training and practical examination must be hands-on with real equipment and specimens, which is why employers pair online theory with onsite practical sessions. See NDT training online.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the classroom hours and experience hours in your employer's written practice, which normally follow the SNT-TC-1A recommendations. Classroom hours can be completed in a few weeks of focused study. Experience hours usually take much longer and depend on how much UT work you actually do. The training requirements matrix lists the recommended hours by method and level.

Do I need a license for radiography in Florida?

The company needs a licence or registration from the Florida Department of Health's Bureau of Radiation Control, and individuals performing industrial radiography must meet the state's radiographer training and certification requirements. NDT RT certification under SNT-TC-1A is a separate credential that covers your ability to perform and interpret the method. You need both to work as a radiographer.

What does NDT training cost in Tampa?

We do not publish prices, because cost depends on the method, level, number of candidates and whether training is online, in a cohort or onsite at your facility. Tell us what you need and you will get a cohort or onsite quote within one business day. Request a Tampa training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Tampa employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used framework for industrial NDT personnel qualification in the United States, and most Tampa Bay industrial, power and marine employers work to it. Remember that SNT-TC-1A certification is employer-based. Your training and experience records transfer, but a new employer recertifies you under its own written practice. Some aerospace employers require NAS 410 instead.

Which NDT method should I learn first for Tampa Bay work?

If you are aiming at plants and terminals, UT is the most requested method. For ship repair, structural steel and crane inspection, MT and VT get you working quickest. Many technicians start with one method, gain experience, then add a second.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Tampa?

No. We deliver live online theory, classroom cohorts at arranged venues, and onsite training at the employer's facility. That is deliberate, because onsite practical training on your own components is more relevant than generic coupons.

Can you train our crew around a planned outage or dry-dock period?

Yes. We usually run theory online in the weeks before an outage and schedule practical sessions for the quieter period afterwards. Give us the outage window and we will plan backwards from it.

I left the military with NDI experience. Can I get civilian certification?

Often, yes. Your employer's Level III decides how much documented military training and experience can be credited under its written practice. Formal SNT-TC-1A classroom training and employer examinations usually close the gap. Bring your records to a Level III consultation.

Do you offer API, CWI or NAS 410 courses?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based only. Some Tampa employers also ask for API inspector, AWS CWI or NAS 410 qualifications, and those are obtained through their own schemes.

How do I prepare for the Level III exams?

Our Level III exam preparation covers the Basic examination and method examinations, with practice questions and a structured study plan.

Ready to plan? Ask about onsite training for your Tampa crew, or browse all NDT training programmes.
